synoptic.summary: A broad Pacific Northwest trough is crossing Utah. Its cold front passes tonight into early Friday with a burst of heavier valley rain and mountain snow. Showers follow through Friday afternoon, fed by cold-pool instability over northern Utah. Snow levels fall to the valley floors late Friday into early Saturday. The forecast discussion expects the surface flow to shift to ~270°–300° on Friday, then back to ~150° in the evening. High pressure crosses Utah Saturday into Sunday with dry, light-wind conditions. A weaker system follows Monday–Tuesday, mainly over southern Utah. Thunder chances stay at 0–5%. Data gaps this run: the winds-aloft forecast (GFS) and the Salt Lake airport pressure/METAR fetch both failed. Rotor and mixing checks therefore rely on the NWS transport wind (mean wind in the mixed layer) and the airport forecasts.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Behind the front, precip will become primarily focused over northern Utah where the best cold pool instability will remain. … Behind the exit trough, confidence is high that high pressure will track across Utah and southwest Wyoming Saturday into Sunday, bringing dry conditions.

pressure.significance: No pressure data this run (Salt Lake airport series empty, METAR fetch timed out). Per the forecast discussion, the trough crosses Friday and high pressure builds Saturday–Sunday. Expect gusty, showery post-frontal flow Friday, then calm conditions.

observations.summary: Thursday evening readings (18:10–18:40 local) are current for the time of this run but about 13 h before the first slot. They show the pre-frontal gradient in charge: flow from 148°–180° at 9–17 kt, with gusts of 18–23 kt at Salt Lake airport and Alpine and 30–36 kt at Lehi. There is no evening switch to 320°–360°. Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data. Spanish Fork and Lehi reported gusts only, with no direction or sustained speed.
